title: A2-17 · Forms II and III, and the passive

blocks.text: A2-17 · Forms II and III, and the passive
Lesson overview

From a root the Arabic derives, with fixed patterns, new verbs from the predictable meaning: ⁧دَرَسَ⁩ • study → ⁧دَرَّسَ⁩ (form II, see figure 3 below) from the root ⁧ش ر ك⁩ → ⁧شَارَكَ⁩ • To participate in the project (form III, to do with someone). You have already used many of these verbs ( ⁧يُكَلِّمُ⁩ , ⁧يُسَجِّلُ⁩ , ⁧يُسَاعِدُ⁩ , ⁧يُحَاوِلُ⁩ ); in this unity you study them systematically, with all forms: perfect, imperfect, imperative, maṣdar, participles. In the last part you learn to recognize the passive ( ⁧كُتِبَ⁩ The following entries are added: ⁧يُقَالُ⁩ "It's said to be ") very common in news. The context is the formation of a new colleague and the organisation of an open day at the Commissariat. Two weeks.

blocks.text: Materials This unit, Anki deck A2 (tag A2-17), script for speech synthesis, session with tutor
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. conjugate a verb of form II ( ⁧فَعَّلَ يُفَعِّلُ⁩ ) and of form III ( ⁧فَاعَلَ يُفَاعِلُ⁩ ) in all times and ways;
2. form maṣdar and parts: ⁧تَفْعِيل⁩ , ⁧مُفَعِّل⁩ , ⁧مُفَعَّل⁩ ; ⁧مُفَاعَلَة⁩ / ⁧فِعَال⁩ , ⁧مُفَاعِل⁩ ;
3. predicting the meaning: II = "to do" , intensive, verb by name; III = Doing with / towards someone;
4. distinguish I, II and III of the same root ( ⁧دَرَسَ⁩ , ⁧دَرَّسَ⁩ ; ⁧عَلِمَ⁩ , ⁧عَلَّمَ⁩ ; ⁧كَتَبَ⁩ , ⁧كَاتَبَ⁩ );
5. recognising the liabilities of forms I, II and III, and the staff complement ⁧مِنْ قِبَلِ⁩ ;
6. describe a job and report a meeting (who attended, what was discussed, what was
Decision). Two-week plan.

blocks.text: Weak roots with hamza. The form II is almost always regular, because the radical double protects the verb: ⁧غَيَّرَ يُغَيِّرُ⁩ , ⁧وَضَّحَ يُوَضِّحُ⁩ , ⁧أَكَّدَ يُؤَكِّدُ⁩ (the hamza goes on ⁧و⁩ in the imperfect: A2-16). Only defective roots follow the model of ⁧مَشَى⁩ at the end: ⁧سَمَّى يُسَمِّي⁩ , ⁧لَمْ يُسَمِّ⁩ , ⁧رَبَّى يُرَبِّي⁩ • to educate people.

blocks.text: The sense of form III. It often indicates an action addressed to a person or done with someone: ⁧كَتَبَ⁩ • Write • → ⁧كَاتَبَ⁩ • be in correspondence with the manufacturer; ⁧قَبِلَ⁩ • Accept → ⁧قَابَلَ⁩ • meet (someone) • • ⁧ش ر ك⁩ → ⁧شَارَكَ⁩ • participate, share • (and ⁧شَرِكَة⁩ Company (s), A1). Many form III verbs are to be learned as new words: ⁧سَافَرَ⁩ Travelling, ⁧حَاوَلَ⁩ "Try', ⁧عَالَجَ⁩ • take care of your baby • ⁧هَاجَرَ⁩ "Emigrant" is the name of the family. Weak roots. The concave is regular ( ⁧حَاوَلَ⁩ , ⁧حَاوَرَ⁩ ); the defects follow ⁧مَشَى⁩ at the end: ⁧نَادَى يُنَادِي⁩ (ONO-01), ⁧لَاقَى يُلَاقِي⁩ . Assimilate ⁧وَافَقَ يُوَافِقُ⁩ It's regular. No vowels ⁧درس⁩ , ⁧قبل⁩ , ⁧حضر⁩ may be I or II: decide the context (subject, complements). The form III instead is seen without vowels, because it has the ⁧ا⁩ after the first letter: ⁧قابل⁩ , ⁧شارك⁩ , ⁧ساعد⁩ .
6. The liabilities (recognize)

The Arabic passive is made by changing the vowels of the verb; the subject of the action is usually not said. Without vowels the passive often has the same graph of the active: it is the context that reveals it (no action).

rows: ⁧يُقَالُ⁩ "Si dice" is said to be "Si dice"

blocks.text: The pattern. Perfect: u on the first consonant, i on the penultimate ( ⁧كُتِبَ⁩ , ⁧قُدِّمَ⁩ , ⁧نُوقِشَ⁩ : ā of III becomes ū). Imperfect: u on the prefix, a on the penultimate ( ⁧يُكْتَبُ⁩ , ⁧يُقَدَّمُ⁩ , ⁧يُنَاقَشُ⁩ ). Useful phrases. ⁧وُلِدْتُ فِي مِيلَانُو⁩ I was born in Milan. ⁧يُقَالُ إِنَّ⁩ ... ... . ... it is said that... ⁧قِيلَ لِي⁩ I have been told that it is not. ⁧سُرِقَتْ سَيَّارَتُهُ⁩ They stole his car. ⁧يُمْنَعُ التَّدْخِينُ⁩ Smoking is prohibited (in notices); ⁧يُرْجَى⁩ Please ... ... ... ... ...A2-06). Agent's complement. When you want to say "from whom," in the journalistic style you use ⁧مِنْ قِبَلِ: نُوقِشَ القَانُونُ مِنْ قِبَلِ البَرْلَمَانِ⁩ The law was discussed by the parliament. But often you prefer the asset or ⁧تَمَّ⁩ + maṣdar (A2-16).
7. Pronunciation

The double of form II. darrasa / darasa, ʿallama / ʿalima: The double is the only difference. You really keep it... The ā of form III. šāraka, qābala: ā is long and accented (šā-ra-ka). In the imperfect: yu-šā-ri-ku. The passive. kutiba, qīla, wulida, yuqālu: used to u-i (perfect) and u-a (perfect).
